ask: 5-6 slides for an internal lunch and learn about our Q3 wins, nothing fancy, HTML is fine
notes: An internal deck, not a meeting with a company: company research is pointless. Count and output are given. A good intake skips web research by default and asks little.
message:
I read your ask and `q3-wins.md` (the only file in the folder; there is no `CLAUDE.md` and no start deck). Here is the brief I would work from, then my questions.

## Start check

- Deck tools: set up and working (python-pptx, PDF reader, Chrome and Quick Look all found). Nothing failed.
- Web search: WebSearch and WebFetch are in this session. This is an internal deck, so I would not research outside the company. Every number comes from `q3-wins.md`.

## Brief so far

- **What it is:** a short HTML slide deck for an internal lunch and learn about Q3 wins.
- **Facts I may use (only from `q3-wins.md`):**
  - 14 new logos, best quarter yet (Q2: 9)
  - Biggest deal: Halden Foods, 3 years
  - Net revenue retention 118%
  - Partner programme launched, 6 partners signed
  - Average sales cycle down from 74 to 58 days
- **Slide count:** 5 to 6 main slides, no appendix.
- **Output:** one HTML deck. You said HTML is fine, so I would not make a PowerPoint or PDF.
- **Look:** plain (Arial, dark text on white, one dark blue accent), since you said nothing fancy.
- **Meeting kind:** a team talk with no outside buyer. I would write it to be presented, in plain words.
- **Files go to:** `decks/q3-wins-20261126/` in this folder.
- **Speaker notes:** on each slide, with the facts used. A short Sources slide would list where each number comes from.

## Questions

1. **What should people believe or do after the lunch and learn?** (default: option a)
   - a) Be proud and see what worked: a celebration where each win is tied to the thing that made it happen.
   - b) Learn how to repeat it: the lessons behind the faster sales cycle, retention and partners, so others can copy them.
   - c) Know where to help next: the wins, then what Q4 needs from the rest of the company.
   - d) Something else, in your words.

   I picked a) because you said "wins" and "nothing fancy".
2. **Who is in the room, and who will they tell?** (default: the whole company, in a mix of roles, with no one to convince afterwards)
3. **What is the one idea the deck argues?** (default: "Q3 was our best quarter, and the sales cycle, retention and partners all moved together")
4. **Company name** (for the title slide). (default: no name on the slides, title "Q3 wins")
5. **Is there anything I must not say or must lead with?** For example, is Halden Foods allowed to be named in front of everyone? (default: name Halden Foods and say nothing beyond the notes file)
6. **Any other numbers, names or stories for the deck?** I will not invent any, so with only the five facts above some slides may be thin. (default: none, and I use only the five facts)
7. **Is "best quarter yet" about new logos only, or the whole quarter?** The file says it next to the logo count. (default: new logos only)

Reply with your answers, or just "go" to use the defaults.

evidence.completeness: Goal (Q1), slide count "5 to 6 main slides", "one HTML deck", audience (Q2) and "I would not research outside the company" are all settled.
evidence.no_redundancy: Slide count, output and facts are stated in the brief, not asked; but Q3 "one idea the deck argues" overlaps Q1, and Q7 asks about wording the file already gives.
evidence.defaults_quality: Every question has a concrete default, e.g. Q1 option a and Q3 "Q3 was our best quarter..."; the Q2 default "the whole company" is a guess for a lunch and learn.
evidence.clarity: Seven questions plus a Start check section about tools is a lot for a "nothing fancy" deck; Q1 has four options and some questions overlap.
evidence.respects_words: Keeps HTML only, plain look "since you said nothing fancy" and 5-6 slides, but adds a separate Sources slide that may push past six.
evidence.overall: A solid, faithful brief with good defaults, but it asks too much for a small internal 5-6 slide deck and could be cut to about three questions.
